components.note: 皮 (skin) — a hand 又 stripping hide from an animal; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī, 坡 pō and 玻 bō.
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑, 胖); 肤 is the skin.
夫 (fū) — same sound — 肤 is fū, like 夫; also in 皮肤.

example.hanzi: 冬天皮肤很容易干燥。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān pífū hěn róngyì gānzào.
example.english: Skin easily gets dry in winter.
example.fact: 皮 alone already means "skin, hide, peel" and applies broadly to people, animals, or fruit alike (苹果皮, "apple peel") — 肤 narrows that general sense specifically to human skin, so 皮肤 fuses a broad root word with a person-specific modifier.

examples.hanzi: 她的皮肤很白,也很光滑。
examples.pinyin: Tā de pífū hěn bái, yě hěn guānghuá.
examples.english: Her skin is very fair and smooth.

examples.hanzi: 夏天出门要小心,别让皮肤晒伤。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān chūmén yào xiǎoxīn, bié ràng pífū shài shāng.
examples.english: Be careful going out in summer so your skin doesn't get sunburned.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 他去年参加了部队。
example.pinyin: Tā qùnián cānjiā le bùduì.
example.english: He joined the army last year.
example.fact: 部队 literally combines 部 ("division, section") with 队 ("team, line") — a division organized into ranks — and doubles today as informal shorthand for "the military" in general, much as English speakers say "the army" to mean military service broadly.

examples.hanzi: 这支部队今天要去山里训练。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī bùduì jīntiān yào qù shān lǐ xùnliàn.
examples.english: This unit is going into the mountains for training today.

examples.hanzi: 部队明天早上五点出发。
examples.pinyin: Bùduì míngtiān zǎoshang wǔ diǎn chūfā.
examples.english: The troops set out at five tomorrow morning.

components.note: 匸 (hiding box) — traditional 區 put several 品 (goods) in a box 匸: separate compartments, hence districts; 区 is area, in 地区.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.hanzi: 这两个词的区别是什么?
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè cí de qūbié shì shénme?
example.english: What's the difference between these two words?
example.fact: 区别 works as both noun ("a difference") and verb ("to distinguish, to tell apart") without changing form at all — a common pattern in Chinese, where the same two-character compound flexibly serves different parts of speech depending on where it lands in the sentence.

examples.hanzi: 你能说出这两个字的区别吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shuō chū zhè liǎng ge zì de qūbié ma?
examples.english: Can you tell the difference between these two characters?

examples.hanzi: 我们要区别对待不同的情况。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào qūbié duìdài bùtóng de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: We should treat different situations differently.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh/body radical (月 in 脸, 脚, 肚); 背 is the back of the body.
北 (běi) — near sound — 背 is bèi; 北 originally pictured two people back to back, which is the sense of 背.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 他总是在背后说别人的坏话。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì zài bèihòu shuō biéren de huàihuà.
example.english: He always talks badly about people behind their backs.
example.fact: 背后 extends its literal spatial sense ("behind, at the back") into the same figurative territory as the English idiom "behind someone's back" — talking about someone 背后 implies secrecy or gossip, a metaphor the two languages happen to share almost exactly.

examples.hanzi: 他躲在门背后,吓了我一跳。
examples.pinyin: Tā duǒ zài mén bèihòu, xià le wǒ yí tiào.
examples.english: He hid behind the door and gave me a scare.

examples.hanzi: 这件事的背后一定有原因。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì de bèihòu yídìng yǒu yuányīn.
examples.english: There must be a reason behind this.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and catching: 罗, 罚, 罪; 置 first meant to set a net, then to place.
直 (zhí) is a near sound match for zhì; same part in 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 这台机器上装有一个安全装置。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì shàng zhuāng yǒu yí gè ānquán zhuāngzhì.
example.english: This machine has a safety device installed on it.
example.fact: 装置 covers both noun ("a device, apparatus") and verb ("to install, to set up"). 装 originally centered on dress and attire (its 衣 "clothing" component) but has drifted to also mean "to install" or even "to pretend," while 置 ("to place, to put") reinforces the placement sense that 装置 relies on today.

examples.hanzi: 这个装置可以自动关灯。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhuāngzhì kěyǐ zìdòng guān dēng.
examples.english: This device can turn off lights automatically.

examples.hanzi: 工人们正在安装一套新的装置。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài ānzhuāng yí tào xīn de zhuāngzhì.
examples.english: The workers are installing a new set of equipment.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.
田 (field) — fields have boundaries, which is what 界 means.
介 (jiè) gives the exact sound; 介 also sounds out 价 jià.

example.hanzi: 这种病毒已经传播到全世界。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú yǐjīng chuánbò dào quánshìjiè.
example.english: This virus has already spread across the entire world.
example.fact: 全世界 stacks two "whole" ideas back to back — 全 ("entire") reinforcing 世界 ("world," itself literally "generations" 世 plus "boundary" 界) — giving the phrase a slightly more emphatic feel than 世界 alone, similar to English occasionally saying "the whole entire world."

examples.hanzi: 这部电影在全世界都很受欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng zài quán shìjiè dōu hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: This movie is popular all over the world.

examples.hanzi: 全世界的孩子都喜欢玩游戏。
examples.pinyin: Quán shìjiè de háizi dōu xǐhuan wán yóuxì.
examples.english: Kids around the world like playing games.

components.note: 木 (wood) — originally 權, the sliding weight of a steelyard scale: weighing, then power; 又 is just a simplification stand-in.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 总统的权力受到宪法的限制。
example.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng de quánlì shòudào xiànfǎ de xiànzhì.
example.english: The president's power is limited by the constitution.
example.fact: 权力 ("power, authority") is a common point of confusion with its near-homophone 权利 — identical pinyin and tones, differing only in the second character (力 "force" vs 利 "benefit"), yet naming two entirely different concepts: the capacity to act versus an entitlement one holds.

examples.hanzi: 没有人有权力随便打开别人的信。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén yǒu quánlì suíbiàn dǎkāi biérén de xìn.
examples.english: No one has the right to open other people's letters.

examples.hanzi: 他当上了经理,手里有了更大的权力。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāng shàng le jīnglǐ, shǒu lǐ yǒu le gèng dà de quánlì.
examples.english: He became manager and gained more power.

components.note: 三 — three strokes, one more than 二. The numbers 一 二 三 are the only ones counted by drawing lines.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — liquids and flow: 河, 汤, 酒; 治 first meant controlling water, then governing and curing.
台 (tái) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 始 shǐ and 胎 tāi.

example.hanzi: 我午饭吃了一个三明治。
example.pinyin: Wǒ wǔfàn chī le yí gè sānmíngzhì.
example.english: I ate a sandwich for lunch.
example.fact: 三明治 is a phonetic transliteration of English "sandwich" — the characters (三 "three," 明 "bright," 治 "govern") were picked purely for their sound and carry no meaningful connection to the food, the same borrowing strategy seen in 罗马 ("Rome") elsewhere in this batch.

examples.hanzi: 早上我常常吃三明治,喝牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang wǒ chángcháng chī sānmíngzhì, hē niúnǎi.
examples.english: In the morning I often eat a sandwich and drink milk.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的三明治又大又便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de sānmíngzhì yòu dà yòu piányi.
examples.english: The sandwiches in this shop are big and cheap.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 木 is wood, as in 桌, 板, 树; 棒 is a stick.
奉 (fèng) — loose hint — 棒 is bàng; 奉 also sounds out 捧 pěng.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 他每个周末都去打棒球。
example.pinyin: Tā měi gè zhōumò dōu qù dǎ bàngqiú.
example.english: He goes to play baseball every weekend.
example.fact: 棒球 is a transparent calque of English "baseball" — 棒 ("a stick, a bat") plus 球 ("ball") — translated by meaning rather than sound, unlike the purely phonetic sports and food loanwords elsewhere in this batch (三明治, "sandwich").

examples.hanzi: 他是一个棒球迷,每场比赛都看。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge bàngqiú mí, měi chǎng bǐsài dōu kàn.
examples.english: He is a baseball fan and watches every game.

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟想学打棒球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi xiǎng xué dǎ bàngqiú.
examples.english: My younger brother wants to learn to play baseball.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 聊 is a chat, with ears open.
卯 (mǎo) is a loose sound clue; same part in 柳 liǔ, 留 liú, 贸 mào.
耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 聊 is a chat, with ears open.
卯 (mǎo) is a loose sound clue; same part in 柳 liǔ, 留 liú, 贸 mào.

example.hanzi: 有空的话,我们聊聊天。
example.pinyin: Yǒu kòng dehuà, wǒmen liáoliao tiān.
example.english: If you have time, let's chat for a bit.
example.fact: 聊聊 reduplicates the single verb 聊 ("to chat") — the same softening pattern seen elsewhere in this deck's 谢谢 (from 谢) — turning a plain verb into a light, casual invitation. In speech it's very often extended to 聊聊天 ("have a little chat"), where 天 functions as a fixed, largely idiomatic object rather than literally meaning "sky."

examples.hanzi: 下班后,我们找个地方聊聊吧。
examples.pinyin: Xiàbān hòu, wǒmen zhǎo ge dìfang liáoliao ba.
examples.english: After work, let's find a place to chat.

examples.hanzi: 我想跟你聊聊昨天的事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ liáoliao zuótiān de shì.
examples.english: I'd like to talk with you about what happened yesterday.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
鱼 (fish) — 鱼 is the fish radical, as in 鲨, 鲸; 鲜 pairs 鱼 with 羊 (sheep) — both freshly tasty foods, so fresh.

example.hanzi: 这些蔬菜看起来很新鲜。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē shūcài kàn qǐlai hěn xīnxiān.
example.english: These vegetables look very fresh.
example.fact: 新鲜 combines 新 ("new") with 鲜 (originally "fresh fish or meat," built from 鱼 "fish" plus 羊 "sheep") — 鲜 alone still carries that food-freshness sense (鲜肉, "fresh meat"), which is why 新鲜 extends naturally to non-food senses like a "fresh" or novel idea, mirroring the same metaphor English makes.

examples.hanzi: 我想买新鲜的水果。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi xīnxiān de shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: I'd like to buy some fresh fruit.

examples.hanzi: 对孩子来说,一切都很新鲜。
examples.pinyin: Duì háizi lái shuō, yíqiè dōu hěn xīnxiān.
examples.english: For a child, everything is new and interesting.

components.note: 工 (work) — a left hand 𠂇 with 工 (work): the hand that helps with work; compare 右 on the right.
口 (mouth) — 右 is a hand 又 plus 口 (mouth) — as a memory aid, the right hand brings food to the mouth; 右 also sounds out 佑 yòu.

example.hanzi: 会议大概三点左右开始。
example.pinyin: Huìyì dàgài sān diǎn zuǒyòu kāishǐ.
example.english: The meeting will start at around three o'clock.
example.fact: Beyond its literal "left and right," 左右 attached after a number becomes Mandarin's all-purpose "approximately" (三点左右, "around 3 o'clock"; 十个左右, "about ten") — the logic being that the true value sits somewhere between a bit to the left and a bit to the right of the stated number.

examples.hanzi: 他五十岁左右,个子不高。
examples.pinyin: Tā wǔshí suì zuǒyòu, gèzi bù gāo.
examples.english: He is around fifty and not very tall.

examples.hanzi: 他们的意见没法左右我的决定。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de yìjiàn méi fǎ zuǒyòu wǒ de juédìng.
examples.english: Their opinions can't sway my decision.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 别担心,你可以放心。
example.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, nǐ kěyǐ fàngxīn.
example.english: Don't worry, you can relax.
example.fact: 放心 literally means "to set down (放) the heart-mind (心)" — the same 心 that anchors 担心 ("to carry worry in the heart") and 关心 ("to care") — Chinese frequently locates emotion physically in 心 much the way English locates it in the "heart," which makes 放心 fairly transparent once you know the character.

examples.hanzi: 你一个人去,我不放心。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yí ge rén qù, wǒ bú fàngxīn.
examples.english: I don't feel at ease with you going alone.

examples.hanzi: 孩子睡着了,你放心吧。
examples.pinyin: Háizi shuì zháo le, nǐ fàngxīn ba.
examples.english: The kid fell asleep, so you can relax.

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 我终于学会了怎么用筷子。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú xuéhuì le zěnme yòng kuàizi.
example.english: I finally learned how to use chopsticks.
example.fact: 学会 pairs 学 ("to study") with 会 in its complement sense "to have mastered, to know how to." 学会 specifically marks the moment a skill is acquired, contrasted with plain 学 (ongoing study) or 会 alone (already knowing how). The same two characters, read as a noun instead, separately mean "institute, learned society."

examples.hanzi: 你什么时候学会骑自行车的?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou xuéhuì qí zìxíngchē de?
examples.english: When did you learn to ride a bicycle?

examples.hanzi: 我想学会做中国菜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xuéhuì zuò Zhōngguó cài.
examples.english: I want to learn to cook Chinese food.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.

example.hanzi: 这个月的水电费很贵。
example.pinyin: Zhège yuè de shuǐdiànfèi hěn guì.
example.english: This month's water and electricity bill is expensive.
example.fact: 费 means both a fee and spending: 学费 (tuition), 免费 (free of charge), 浪费 (to waste), 小费 (tip). 费劲 means to take much effort. It is also a surname (Fèi).

examples.hanzi: 上学要交很多费用。
examples.pinyin: Shàngxué yào jiāo hěn duō fèiyòng.
examples.english: Going to school costs a lot of fees.

examples.hanzi: 他花了很多钱，觉得很浪费。
examples.pinyin: Tā huā le hěn duō qián, juéde hěn làngfèi.
examples.english: He spent a lot of money and felt it was wasteful.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 疼; 痕 is the scar a sore leaves.
艮 (gèn) — near sound — 痕 is hén; 艮 also sounds out 根 gēn and 很 hěn.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迹 is a footprint, as in 奇迹 miracle.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 迹 is jì; 亦 also sounds out 迹 jì.

example.hanzi: 墙上还留着火灾的痕迹。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng hái liú zhe huǒzāi de hénjì.
example.english: Traces of the fire are still left on the wall.
example.fact: 痕 (built on 疒, "sickness") originally named a scar left by injury, while 迹 (built on 辶, "to walk") named a footprint or trail left by walking — 痕迹 fuses "scar" and "footprint" into one word for any lingering trace, whether physical damage or a path once taken.

examples.hanzi: 雪地上留下了他的脚印痕迹。
examples.pinyin: Xuědì shang liúxià le tā de jiǎoyìn hénjì.
examples.english: His footprints left marks in the snow.

examples.hanzi: 岁月在她脸上留下了痕迹。
examples.pinyin: Suìyuè zài tā liǎn shang liúxià le hénjì.
examples.english: Time has left its traces on her face.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 稳 is firm, steady, like a solid harvest.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 他现在有一份稳定的工作。
example.pinyin: Tā xiànzài yǒu yí fèn wěndìng de gōngzuò.
example.english: He now has a stable job.
example.fact: 稳 pictures a heavy, ripe stalk of grain (禾) standing firm rather than swaying — 稳定 extends that image of settled grain to anything that holds steady, whether a job, a market, or an emotional state (情绪稳定, "emotionally stable").

examples.hanzi: 我希望能有一份稳定的工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng néng yǒu yí fèn wěndìng de gōngzuò.
examples.english: I hope to have a stable job.

examples.hanzi: 他的情绪不太稳定。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qíngxù bú tài wěndìng.
examples.english: His mood is not very stable.

components.note: 酋 (wine jar) with a hand 寸 offering it: honoring a guest. 尊 sounds out 遵 zūn (obey) and 樽 zūn (goblet).
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放; 敬 is respectful behaviour, as in 尊敬.
苟 (gǒu) — sound clue is weak — 敬 is jìng, but 敬 sounds out 警 jǐng.

example.hanzi: 我们都很尊敬这位老师。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu hěn zūnjìng zhè wèi lǎoshī.
example.english: We all really respect this teacher.
example.fact: 尊 pictures a jar of wine (酋) offered up with both hands (寸) — a gesture of formal respect toward elders or superiors — while 敬 independently carries the same reverence. 尊敬 is generally reserved for people, whereas the broader 尊重 ("to respect") can also apply to opinions, rules, or feelings.

examples.hanzi: 我很尊敬我的老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn zūnjìng wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: I respect my teacher very much.

examples.hanzi: 对长辈要尊敬,这是我们的习惯。
examples.pinyin: Duì zhǎngbèi yào zūnjìng, zhè shì wǒmen de xíguàn.
examples.english: We should respect elders, it's our custom.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — marks rivers, liquids and anything that flows, as in 海 sea, 汤 soup, 酒 liquor.
可 (kě) hints at the sound — 河 is hé; 可 also sounds out 歌 gē and 何 hé.

example.hanzi: 河里有很多鱼。
example.pinyin: Hé lǐ yǒu hěn duō yú.
example.english: There are many fish in the river.
example.fact: 河 was originally the proper name of the Yellow River (黄河), while 江 was the Yangtze. Now it means any river, with the measure word 条, and appears in 银河 (the Milky Way, "silver river").

examples.hanzi: 这条河很宽，船可以通过。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé hěn kuān, chuán kěyǐ tōngguò.
examples.english: This river is wide enough for boats to pass.

examples.hanzi: 我们在河边散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài hébiān sànbù.
examples.english: We are taking a walk by the river.

components.note: 司 (sī) is a sound clue for 词 cí and 饲 sì; as a word it means to manage, as in 公司 company.

example.hanzi: 他在一家小公司工作。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā xiǎo gōngsī gōngzuò.
example.english: He works at a small company.
example.fact: 司 is a bound form: 公司 (company), 司机 (driver), 司法 (judiciary), 上司 (boss). Its original sense is to take charge of something.

examples.hanzi: 这个公司有三百个员工。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gōngsī yǒu sānbǎi gè yuángōng.
examples.english: This company has three hundred employees.

examples.hanzi: 他是一名火车司机。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng huǒchē sījī.
examples.english: He is a train driver.

components.note: 匸 (hiding box) — traditional 區 put several 品 (goods) in a box 匸: separate compartments, hence districts; 区 is area, in 地区.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth and land, as in 地, 城; 域 is a territory.
或 (huò) — near sound — 域 is yù; 或 also sounds out 惑 huò.

example.hanzi: 这个区域禁止停车。
example.pinyin: Zhège qūyù jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
example.english: Parking is prohibited in this area.
example.fact: 区域 doubles up two near-synonymous "bounded space" characters — 区 (a fenced-off territory) and 域 (a plot of land marked by boundaries, built on 土 "earth") — the same root 区 also anchors 区别 elsewhere in this batch, though there it means "distinction" rather than "territory."

examples.hanzi: 这个区域是安静区,请不要说话。
examples.pinyin: Zhège qūyù shì ānjìng qū, qǐng bú yào shuōhuà.
examples.english: This area is a quiet zone, so please don't talk.

examples.hanzi: 这个区域经常下雨。
examples.pinyin: Zhège qūyù jīngcháng xiàyǔ.
examples.english: It often rains in this area.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 城; hard like packed earth. Top part simplifies 臤 (hard), also in 紧 jǐn and 贤 xián.
弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.

example.hanzi: 她在困难面前表现得很坚强。
example.pinyin: Tā zài kùnnan miànqián biǎoxiàn de hěn jiānqiáng.
example.english: She showed great strength in the face of difficulty.
example.fact: 坚强 typically describes inner, emotional or moral strength — a strong-willed person who doesn't break under pressure — while physical strength usually reaches for a different word, 强壮 (of the body) or 有力 (of a grip or force), a distinction English's single adjective "strong" doesn't make.

examples.hanzi: 她是一个坚强的女人,从不轻易放弃。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge jiānqiáng de nǚrén, cóng bù qīngyì fàngqì.
examples.english: She is a strong woman who never gives up easily.

examples.hanzi: 虽然很难过,他还是坚强地站了起来。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn nánguò, tā háishi jiānqiáng de zhàn le qǐlái.
examples.english: Although he was very sad, he stood up strongly.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.

example.hanzi: 这些数据显示销量在上升。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē shùjù xiǎnshì xiāoliàng zài shàngshēng.
example.english: This data shows that sales are rising.
example.fact: 据 alone means "evidence, basis" (its 扌 "hand" component evokes grasping something as proof) — 数据 literally means "numerical evidence," a word that entered modern Chinese to translate the Western mathematical and statistical concept of "data," later extending naturally to computing.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要更多的数据来做判断。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào gèng duō de shùjù lái zuò pànduàn.
examples.english: We need more data to make a judgment.

examples.hanzi: 这份数据已经保存在电脑里了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn shùjù yǐjīng bǎocún zài diànnǎo lǐ le.
examples.english: This data has already been saved on the computer.

components.note: 王 (jade) — 王 on the left is 玉 (jade), as in 球, 现, 玩; 玻璃 glass was named like a precious stone.
皮 (pí) — near sound — 玻 is bō; 皮 also sounds out 坡 pō and 波 bō.
王 (jade) — 王 on the left is 玉 (jade), as in 球, 现, 玩; 璃 is a glassy stone, as in 玻璃.
离 (lí) — same sound — 璃 is lí, like 离.

example.hanzi: 小心,这个杯子是玻璃做的。
example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhège bēizi shì bōli zuò de.
example.english: Be careful, this cup is made of glass.
example.fact: 玻璃 is a rare case where both characters share the same 王 (jade) semantic component yet neither carries independent meaning outside this word — 玻 and 璃 exist almost solely to spell "glass," a treatment more typical of foreign loanwords than native vocabulary.

examples.hanzi: 这扇窗户的玻璃坏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shàn chuānghu de bōli huài le.
examples.english: The glass of this window is broken.

examples.hanzi: 地上都是碎玻璃,别过去。
examples.pinyin: Dì shang dōu shì suì bōli, bié guòqù.
examples.english: The ground is covered in broken glass, don't go over.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 力 marks strength and effort, as in 办, 动, 努, 助; 勇 is strength in action, courage.
甬 (yǒng) — same sound — 勇 is yǒng, like 甬; 甬 also sounds out 通 tōng, 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 她终于有勇气告诉父母真相。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú yǒu yǒngqì gàosu fùmǔ zhēnxiàng.
example.english: She finally had the courage to tell her parents the truth.
example.fact: 勇气 pairs 勇 ("brave," built from 力 "strength" plus phonetic 甬, an exact sound match) with 气 ("qi, vital energy") — literally "brave energy," treating courage the way several Chinese compounds treat emotions and mental states: as a form of 气 that can be summoned or run out of (没气了, "out of steam").

examples.hanzi: 你需要一点儿勇气,才能说出自己的想法。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xūyào yìdiǎnr yǒngqì, cái néng shuō chū zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: You need a bit of courage to say what you think.

examples.hanzi: 他很有勇气,敢一个人面对困难。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu yǒngqì, gǎn yí ge rén miànduì kùnnan.
examples.english: He is very brave and dares to face difficulties alone.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁, 钟; mirrors were polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 镜 is jìng; 竟 also sounds out 境 jìng.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的第一个镜头拍得非常美。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de dì yī gè jìngtóu pāi de fēicháng měi.
example.english: The first shot of this movie was filmed beautifully.
example.fact: 镜头 combines 镜 ("mirror," originally polished bronze, 钅) with 头 ("head, tip") — "the tip of the mirror" names the physical lens on a camera, and by extension came to mean an individual filmed shot, the same way English "shot" names both a camera action and its resulting clip.

examples.hanzi: 摄影师把镜头对准了孩子的脸。
examples.pinyin: Shèyǐngshī bǎ jìngtóu duìzhǔn le háizi de liǎn.
examples.english: The photographer pointed the lens at the child's face.

examples.hanzi: 这个镜头里的风景很美。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìngtóu lǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měi.
examples.english: The scenery in this shot is beautiful.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.
工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.

example.hanzi: 公司为员工提供免费午餐。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī wèi yuángōng tígōng miǎnfèi wǔcān.
example.english: The company provides free lunch for its employees.
example.fact: 员工 fuses 员 ("a person holding a role," as in 演员 "actor" or 服务员 "waiter") with 工 ("worker, labor") into a catch-all term covering everyone on a company's payroll, without distinguishing rank the way 职员 (office staff specifically) or 工人 (manual laborer specifically) do.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司有两百多名员工。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu liǎng bǎi duō míng yuángōng.
examples.english: This company has over two hundred employees.

examples.hanzi: 新员工下周一开始上班。
examples.pinyin: Xīn yuángōng xià zhōuyī kāishǐ shàngbān.
examples.english: The new employee starts work next Monday.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and joining, as in 听, 聪, 闻: 联 first meant ears joined, so to link. The part 关 stands in for the traditional shape.
皿 (dish) — 皿 is a dish or vessel, as in 盘, 盒, 盛; oaths were sworn over a sacrificial vessel.
明 (míng) — near sound — 盟 is méng.

example.hanzi: 这两个国家签订了军事联盟。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè guójiā qiāndìng le jūnshì liánméng.
example.english: These two countries signed a military alliance.
example.fact: 盟 pictures an oath sworn over a sacrificial dish (皿) — an image straight out of ancient Chinese covenant ceremonies — and 联 ("to link, to connect") joins it to name any formal alliance, whether ancient states swearing blood oaths or modern countries signing treaties.

examples.hanzi: 这个联盟有十个成员国。
examples.pinyin: Zhège liánméng yǒu shí ge chéngyuán guó.
examples.english: This alliance has ten member countries.

examples.hanzi: 几家公司组成了一个联盟。
examples.pinyin: Jǐ jiā gōngsī zǔchéng le yí ge liánméng.
examples.english: Several companies formed an alliance.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.

example.hanzi: 请保护好你的眼睛。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎohù hǎo nǐ de yǎnjing.
example.english: Please protect your eyes.
example.fact: 保 forms 保护 (to protect), 保证 (to guarantee), 保险 (insurance), 保持 (to keep, maintain) and 保安 (security guard). 请多保重 is a warm farewell meaning "please take good care of yourself".

examples.hanzi: 请保持安静。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎochí ānjìng.
examples.english: Please keep quiet.

examples.hanzi: 我保证明天一定来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎozhèng míngtiān yídìng lái.
examples.english: I promise I will come tomorrow.

meanings: measure word for doors and windows

components.note: 户 (door) — a door 户 with feathers 羽: 扇 is a fan, or a door panel that swings, as in 扇子 fan.

example.hanzi: 房间里有一扇大窗户。
example.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ yǒu yí shàn dà chuānghu.
example.english: There is a big window in the room.
example.fact: 扇 is the measure word for doors and windows: 一扇门, 一扇窗. As a noun 扇子 is a hand fan, and the verb "to fan" is read shān: 扇风, 扇耳光 (to slap someone's face).

examples.hanzi: 他手里拿着一把扇子。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒu lǐ ná zhe yì bǎ shànzi.
examples.english: He is holding a fan in his hand.

examples.hanzi: 请关上那扇门。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng guānshàng nà shàn mén.
examples.english: Please close that door.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阴, 院, 队; 阳 is the sunny side of a hill, with 日 sun.
日 (sun) — 日 is the sun, as in 明, 晴, 时.
火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.

example.hanzi: 今天的阳光特别好。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de yángguāng tèbié hǎo.
example.english: Today's sunshine is especially nice.
example.fact: 阳光 literally means "yang light" — 阳 being the bright, active half of the classical yin-yang (阴阳) pairing — and the word has picked up a modern extension describing an upbeat, warm personality (阳光男孩, "a sunny, positive guy"), the same metaphor English makes when calling someone's disposition "sunny."

examples.hanzi: 阳光从窗户照进房间。
examples.pinyin: Yángguāng cóng chuānghu zhào jìn fángjiān.
examples.english: Sunlight shines into the room through the window.

examples.hanzi: 她是一个阳光的女孩,总是笑着。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge yángguāng de nǚhái, zǒngshì xiào zhe.
examples.english: She is a sunny girl who is always smiling.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.

example.hanzi: 小孩子对什么都很好奇。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi duì shénme dōu hěn hàoqí.
example.english: Children are curious about everything.
example.fact: 好奇 pairs 好 in its less-common fourth-tone reading hào ("to be fond of," as in 好客) with 奇 ("strange, odd") — literally "fond of the strange," a fitting origin for a word meaning "curious." The far more frequent reading of 好, hǎo ("good"), is a different word entirely, so 好奇 is a small tone trap for learners who've only met 好 as hǎo.

examples.hanzi: 我对这个新玩具很好奇。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhège xīn wánjù hěn hàoqí.
examples.english: I'm curious about this new toy.

examples.hanzi: 他好奇地打开了那个盒子。
examples.pinyin: Tā hàoqí de dǎkāi le nàge hézi.
examples.english: He opened that box curiously.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; 审 is a hearing held in a hall.
申 (shēn) is a near sound match for shěn; also in 神 shén, 伸 shēn.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; 判 is to cut in half, so to separate and decide.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 判 is pàn; 半 means half.

example.hanzi: 法庭对他进行了审判。
example.pinyin: Fǎtíng duì tā jìnxíngle shěnpàn.
example.english: The court put him on trial.
example.fact: 审 ("to examine closely," as in 审查) and 判 ("to judge, decide," as in 判断) combine transparently into "examine and judge" — a two-step compositional image that maps almost exactly onto what a trial actually is.

examples.hanzi: 法官今天对这个案子进行审判。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān jīntiān duì zhège ànzi jìnxíng shěnpàn.
examples.english: The judge is holding the trial for this case today.

examples.hanzi: 这次审判持续了三天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shěnpàn chíxù le sān tiān.
examples.english: The trial lasted three days.

components.note: 子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.hanzi: 她一个人完成了这个项目,真了不起。
example.pinyin: Tā yí gè rén wánchéngle zhège xiàngmù, zhēn liǎobuqǐ.
example.english: She finished this project all by herself — that's really amazing.
example.fact: 了不起 uses the same "verb + 不起" potential-complement pattern behind 对不起 ("sorry," literally "cannot face [you]") and 买不起 ("can't afford," literally "cannot rise to buying") — here 了 ("to finish, come to an end") is the thing that "cannot be gotten past," giving 了不起 its sense of being unsurpassed, extraordinary.

examples.hanzi: 这个小孩才五岁就会弹钢琴,真了不起!
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎohái cái wǔ suì jiù huì tán gāngqín, zhēn liǎobuqǐ!
examples.english: This kid can play piano at only five, which is amazing!

examples.hanzi: 他觉得自己是个了不起的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ shì ge liǎobuqǐ de rén.
examples.english: He thinks he is a great person.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.hanzi: 我觉得有点冷。
example.pinyin: Wǒ juéde yǒudiǎn lěng.
example.english: I feel a bit cold.
example.fact: 觉得 (juéde) is the everyday way to say "I feel / I think" and softens opinions: 我觉得很好. The same character is read jiào in 睡觉 (to sleep) and 午觉 (nap), a classic reading pair. 感觉 means feeling.

examples.hanzi: 你觉得这个电影怎么样？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ juéde zhège diànyǐng zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: What do you think of this movie?

examples.hanzi: 我昨晚没睡好，现在觉得很困。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn méi shuìhǎo, xiànzài juéde hěn kùn.
examples.english: I didn't sleep well last night and feel very sleepy now.

meanings: base (of operations, industrial, military, research etc)

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 这里曾经是一个军事基地。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ céngjīng shì yí gè jūnshì jīdì.
example.english: This used to be a military base.
example.fact: 基 alone means "foundation" (as in 基础, "basis") and 地 means "ground, place" — 基地 combines the two into a fairly literal "foundation-ground," the fixed operational site a military, industrial, or research effort is built on.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的生产基地在上海。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de shēngchǎn jīdì zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: This company's production base is in Shanghai.

examples.hanzi: 这里是我们的研究基地。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ shì wǒmen de yánjiū jīdì.
examples.english: This is our research base.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.

example.hanzi: 让我们假设这个理论是对的。
example.pinyin: Ràng wǒmen jiǎshè zhège lǐlùn shì duì de.
example.english: Let's suppose this theory is correct.
example.fact: 假 here keeps its core sense "false, not real" (as in 假的, "fake") rather than its unrelated second reading jià ("vacation," as in 放假) — 假设 literally "to set up something not [yet] real," a vivid image for proposing a hypothesis.

examples.hanzi: 假设你有一百万,你会做什么?
examples.pinyin: Jiǎshè nǐ yǒu yì bǎi wàn, nǐ huì zuò shénme?
examples.english: Suppose you had a million, what would you do?

examples.hanzi: 我们先做一个假设,再来验证它。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān zuò yí ge jiǎshè, zài lái yànzhèng tā.
examples.english: Let's make an assumption first, and then verify it.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones and minerals, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 磨 grind; 砍 is chopping, as with a stone axe.
欠 (qiàn) — loose sound hint (kǎn vs qiàn).

example.hanzi: 他用斧头砍树。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng fǔtóu kǎn shù.
example.english: He chops the tree down with an axe.
example.fact: 砍 is to chop with a blade: 砍柴 (to chop firewood), 砍树 (to fell a tree). In shopping slang 砍价 means to haggle the price down, and online sellers have turned this into group "price cutting" in apps.

examples.hanzi: 他用刀砍断了绳子。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng dāo kǎnduàn le shéngzi.
examples.english: He cut the rope with a knife.

examples.hanzi: 工人们在山上砍树。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zài shān shang kǎn shù.
examples.english: The workers are cutting down trees on the mountain.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 聊 is a chat, with ears open.
卯 (mǎo) is a loose sound clue; same part in 柳 liǔ, 留 liú, 贸 mào.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 我们常常在网上聊天。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chángcháng zài wǎngshàng liáotiān.
example.english: We often chat online.
example.fact: 天 in 聊天 doesn't mean "sky" or "day" here — it's a fossilized object noun bound to the verb 聊 ("to chat") that can't be swapped for a near-synonym, much like 架 is permanently fixed as the object of 打 in 打架 (also in this batch).

examples.hanzi: 晚饭后,我喜欢和妈妈聊天。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnfàn hòu, wǒ xǐhuan hé māma liáotiān.
examples.english: After dinner, I like chatting with my mom.

examples.hanzi: 上课的时候不要聊天。
examples.pinyin: Shàngkè de shíhou bú yào liáotiān.
examples.english: Don't chat during class.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 除了他之外,大家都同意了。
example.pinyin: Chúle tā zhī wài, dàjiā dōu tóngyì le.
example.english: Except for him, everyone agreed.
example.fact: 之外 almost always closes out a "除了...之外" frame ("except for..."), and its 之 is the same literary possessive/linking particle behind 之前 ("before") and 之后 ("after") — a small family of formal, book-language location and time words built the same way.

examples.hanzi: 除了价格之外,质量也很重要。
examples.pinyin: Chúle jiàgé zhī wài, zhìliàng yě hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Besides price, quality matters too.

examples.hanzi: 这件事在我的想象之外。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì zài wǒ de xiǎngxiàng zhī wài.
examples.english: This is beyond my imagination.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female traits, as in 妈, 姐, 妒; 嫉 is jealousy.
疾 (jí) — same sound — 嫉 is jí, like 疾.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female traits, as in 嫉, 妈; 妒 is jealousy.
户 (hù) — loose hint — 妒 is dù; 户 also sounds out 护 hù.

example.hanzi: 他非常嫉妒同事的成功。
example.pinyin: Tā fēicháng jídù tóngshì de chénggōng.
example.english: He's extremely jealous of his colleague's success.
example.fact: 嫉 and 妒 each independently mean "jealous, envious" on their own — 嫉妒 doubles up two near-synonymous characters into one word, the same word-building strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该 elsewhere in this deck.

examples.hanzi: 她嫉妒姐姐有很多朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā jídù jiějie yǒu hěn duō péngyou.
examples.english: She is jealous that her sister has many friends.

examples.hanzi: 你不要嫉妒别人,做好自己就行。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào jídù biérén, zuòhǎo zìjǐ jiù xíng.
examples.english: Don't envy others, just do your best.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 借 is a deal between people, as in 借口.
昔 (xī) — near sound — 借 is jiè; 昔 also sounds out 惜 xī and 错 cuò.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 他总是找借口不来上班。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì zhǎo jièkǒu bù lái shàngbān.
example.english: He's always finding excuses not to come to work.
example.fact: 借 means "to borrow" and 口 means "mouth, something said" — 借口 is literally a "borrowed word," a vivid image of reaching for someone else's ready-made line instead of stating your real reason.

examples.hanzi: 别拿天气当借口,你就是不想去。
examples.pinyin: Bié ná tiānqì dāng jièkǒu, nǐ jiù shì bù xiǎng qù.
examples.english: Don't use the weather as an excuse, you just don't want to go.

examples.hanzi: 他以身体不舒服为借口,没来开会。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐ shēntǐ bù shūfu wéi jièkǒu, méi lái kāihuì.
examples.english: He used feeling unwell as an excuse to skip the meeting.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a lump of earth on the ground; as a radical it marks land and soil, as in 地, 城, 块, 墙.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 这片土地非常肥沃。
example.pinyin: Zhè piàn tǔdì fēicháng féiwò.
example.english: This land is very fertile.
example.fact: 土 and 地 both independently mean "earth, ground" — 土地 doubles up two near-synonymous "earth" characters into one word, the same pattern the pilot batch noted for 喜欢 and 应该.

examples.hanzi: 农民们在土地上种了很多玉米。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmínmen zài tǔdì shang zhòng le hěn duō yùmǐ.
examples.english: The farmers planted a lot of corn on the land.

examples.hanzi: 这块土地是他爷爷留下来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài tǔdì shì tā yéye liú xiàlái de.
examples.english: This piece of land was left by his grandfather.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.

example.hanzi: 这条路很平。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù hěn píng.
example.english: This road is very flat.
example.fact: 平 means flat, level and by extension calm: 和平 (peace), 平安 (safe and sound), 平均 (average), 平时 (usually). 水平 is the level of an ability, as in 汉语水平 (Chinese level).

examples.hanzi: 这块地很平整。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dì hěn píngzhěng.
examples.english: This piece of land is very flat.

examples.hanzi: 今天是平安夜。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì Píng'ānyè.
examples.english: Today is Christmas Eve.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female roles, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 姑 aunt; 姆 is a nanny, as in 保姆.
母 (mǔ) — same sound — 姆 is mǔ, just like 母 (mother).

example.hanzi: 我们请了一位保姆照顾孩子。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen qǐngle yí wèi bǎomǔ zhàogù háizi.
example.english: We hired a nanny to take care of the children.
example.fact: 姆 is a fairly rare character in modern Mandarin, surviving mainly in 保姆 and a small number of classical or dialectal words for a female caretaker — a case where an entire character's everyday use has narrowed down to almost a single word.

examples.hanzi: 保姆每天下午带孩子去公园。
examples.pinyin: Bǎomǔ měi tiān xiàwǔ dài háizi qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: The nanny takes the child to the park every afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 这位保姆做饭做得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi bǎomǔ zuòfàn zuò de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This nanny cooks very well.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摇 is to shake or rock.
䍃 (yáo) — same sound — 摇 is yáo; 䍃 also sounds out 谣 yáo and 遥 yáo.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 滚 is to roll like boiling water.
衮 (gǔn) — same sound — 滚 is gǔn, like 衮.

example.hanzi: 他很喜欢听摇滚音乐。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan tīng yáogǔn yīnyuè.
example.english: He really likes listening to rock music.
example.fact: 摇滚 is a phono-semantic loan translation of English "rock (and) roll" — 摇 ("to shake, sway") and 滚 ("to roll") were picked because their literal meanings echo the physical feel of the English term, not because Chinese needed brand-new native characters for the genre.

examples.hanzi: 他的乐队演奏的是摇滚。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yuèduì yǎnzòu de shì yáogǔn.
examples.english: His band plays rock music.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸年轻的时候是摇滚迷。
examples.pinyin: Bàba niánqīng de shíhou shì yáogǔn mí.
examples.english: Dad was a rock fan when he was young.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 妈妈慢慢放手,让孩子自己走。
example.pinyin: Māma mànmàn fàngshǒu, ràng háizi zìjǐ zǒu.
example.english: The mother slowly let go, letting the child walk on her own.
example.fact: 放手 is literally "to release the hand" (放 "to release" + 手 "hand"), and like English "let go" it spans both the physical action and the figurative sense of giving someone free rein or giving up a struggle.

examples.hanzi: 你该放手了,让他自己做决定。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gāi fàngshǒu le, ràng tā zìjǐ zuò juédìng.
examples.english: It's time to let go and let him make his own decision.

examples.hanzi: 老板终于放手,让年轻人去做这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn zhōngyú fàngshǒu, ràng niánqīngrén qù zuò zhège xiàngmù.
examples.english: The boss finally gave them a free hand and let the young people do this project.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 抱 is to hug or hold in the arms.
包 (bāo) is a close sound clue for bào; it also sounds out 跑 pǎo, 饱 bǎo and 炮 pào.
心 (heart) — 心 marks emotions, as in 怕, 想, 怒; 怨 is a grudge in the heart.
夗 (wǎn) — near sound — 怨 is yuàn.

example.hanzi: 他总是抱怨工作太累。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì bàoyuàn gōngzuò tài lèi.
example.english: He always complains that work is too tiring.
example.fact: 抱 keeps its core sense "to hold, embrace" (as in 抱着孩子, "holding a child"), so 抱怨 literally pictures someone "holding onto" 怨 (a grievance) rather than letting it go — a vivid image behind the everyday word for complaining.

examples.hanzi: 别抱怨了,我们一起想办法吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié bàoyuàn le, wǒmen yìqǐ xiǎng bànfǎ ba.
examples.english: Stop complaining, let's think of a solution together.

examples.hanzi: 她从来不抱怨生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā cónglái bú bàoyuàn shēnghuó.
examples.english: She never complains about life.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 上课的时候要集中注意力。
example.pinyin: Shàngkè de shíhou yào jízhōng zhùyìlì.
example.english: You need to focus your attention during class.
example.fact: 注意力 builds on the two-character verb 注意 ("to pay attention," literally "to pour [one's] mind into something") by adding 力 ("strength, power") to turn the action into the noun naming the mental faculty itself — the same "verb + 力" pattern behind 理解力 ("comprehension") and 想象力 ("imagination").

examples.hanzi: 手机会分散孩子的注意力。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī huì fēnsàn háizi de zhùyìlì.
examples.english: Phones can distract children's attention.

examples.hanzi: 他的注意力很难集中。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhùyìlì hěn nán jízhōng.
examples.english: It's hard for him to concentrate.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the hand family: 打, 拿, 拉. 承 is usually explained as hands lifting something, to bear or accept (承认 admit, 承诺 promise).
又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".

example.hanzi: 这座桥能承受很大的重量。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo néng chéngshòu hěn dà de zhòngliàng.
example.english: This bridge can bear a great deal of weight.
example.fact: 承 and 受 both independently carry a sense of "to receive" — 承 pictures hands lifting something from below, 受 pictures one hand passing something to another — together they form a word for withstanding pressure, whether physical, financial, or emotional.

examples.hanzi: 这张桌子只能承受二十公斤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi zhǐ néng chéngshòu èrshí gōngjīn.
examples.english: This table can only bear twenty kilograms.

examples.hanzi: 她承受了太多压力。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngshòu le tài duō yālì.
examples.english: She has borne too much pressure.
